nodes_add.name: Dravidar Kazhagam
nodes_add.note: Justice Party renamed Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944 under Periyar (his term as leader from 27 August 1944); demanded Dravida Nadu; led by Maniammai from 25 December 1973 and K. Veeramani from 16 March 1978.

nodes_add.name: C. N. Annadurai
nodes_add.note: Periyar's lieutenant in the Dravidar Kazhagam; b. 15 September 1909 Kanchipuram, d. 3 February 1969 Madras; broke with Periyar after the Maniammai marriage and founded the DMK on 17 September 1949; as Chief Minister (1967-69) his government legalised self-respect marriages in 1967.

nodes_update.name: Periyar (E. V. Ramasamy)
nodes_update.note: b. 17 Sept 1879 Erode; Congress 1919-1925; Vaikom satyagraha 1924 (jailed twice); Self-Respect Movement and Kudi Arasu 1925; title Periyar 13 Nov 1938; Justice Party 1939; Dravidar Kazhagam 27 Aug 1944; married Maniammai 9 July 1949; d. 24 Dec 1973 Vellore.

edges_upsert.note: Congress member 1919-1925; left over communal representation at Kanchipuram, 1925; met Gandhi in 1927 (Bangalore per Wikipedia) with three demands, destruction of the Congress, of Hindu religion and of Brahmin domination, and was dissatisfied (Periyar's account, via P. A. Krishnan, Outlook 2019); attacked Gandhi for the rest of his life, though he proposed renaming India Gandhi Desh after the assassination.

Annihilation of Caste translated into Tamil with Periyar's help and published 1937, segments in Kudi Arasu (Wikipedia); first met in Bombay, January 1940 (6 or 8 January in different accounts), again in Madras 1944 (V. Geetha, Forward Press 2017). Alliance of anti-caste thinkers more than teacher and pupil; Periyar did not follow Ambedkar into Buddhism.
Founder-leader from 27 August 1944 until his death in 1973.
Annadurai worked under Periyar in the Justice Party and DK; split after the 9 July 1949 marriage and founded the DMK, 17 September 1949 (The News Minute).

glossary.def: Self-respect. The name of Periyar's movement, founded in 1925, against caste, priesthood and religious authority.
Association or federation, as in Dravidar Kazhagam (Dravidian Federation) and the parties that grew from it.
The usual Tamil name for Ganesha, the elephant-headed god.
"The great one." An honorific given to E. V. Ramasamy by a women's conference in Madras on 13 November 1938.
A wedding without a Brahmin priest, sacred fire or rituals that subordinate the wife, conducted by an exchange of vows and garlands; legalised in the state in 1967.

periyar.mdx: marriage to Maniammai dated 9 July 1949 (Feminism in India; The News Minute places his announcement on 28 June 1949 and the DMK split on 17 September 1949). Wikipedia gives 9 July 1948 in one section and 1949 in another; the unit brief said 1948. The entry uses 1949 and notes the 1948 variant.

periyar.mdx: the brief mentions '1956 image-breaking'. Sources checked separate two events: the Pillaiyar (Ganesha) image-breaking call of 1953 (dated 27 May, Buddha Purnima, in Bala Jeyaraman's biography, seen only through Goodreads highlights) and the burning of pictures of Rama on the Marina in 1956 (Wikipedia, which also mentions an arrest for this in 1955). A primary or newspaper source for both dates would help.

periyar.mdx: the 'snake and Brahmin' saying is widely attributed to Periyar (Wikipedia records the accusation with a Tamil phrase); I could not trace it to a dated speech or text and say so in the entry. Fact-checker may wish to confirm whether any scholarly source locates it.

periyar.mdx: the 'barbarian language' remark is quoted from Wikipedia's translation ('I say Tamil as barbarian language'); Wikipedia's sub-article tags the claim 'better source needed'. Year and original publication not established.

A later Supreme Court notice on a similar plea (LiveLaw) was seen in search results only and is not mentioned.

periyar.mdx: the 1959 Brahmin quotation and the 1973 'annihilation' list come from P. A. Krishnan, a critic, in his own translation (pakrishnan.com 2018; Outlook 2019). Original Tamil sources not seen.

periyar.mdx: Ambedkar link. Tamil translation 1937 per Wikipedia (some accounts say 1936 serialisation in Kudi Arasu). The 6 January 1940 Bombay meeting rests on a single Ambedkarite blog (drambedkarbooks.com). A 1954 trip to Burma for a Buddhist celebration (indianetzone) was not confirmed and is left out.

periyar: Born 17 September 1879, Erode; died 24 December 1973 (Vellore per infobox); Congress 1919-1925; Kashi 1904 choultry story; Vaikom arrival April 1924 and 'Vaikom Veerar' 1925; Kudi Arasu 1925; anti-Hindi jail 1938, Justice Party leadership 1939; 1956 Rama picture burning (also 1955); 1957 call to burn the Constitution, six months; Nehru letter 5 Nov 1957; 'barbarian language' -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar

Left Congress at Kanchipuram conference 1925 after president Thiru V.Ka refused his communal-representation resolution; Cheranmadevi Gurukulam separate seating -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periyar_and_the_Indian_National_Congress
Vaikom satyagraha 30 March 1924 to 23 November 1925; Periyar imprisoned twice; Gandhi's March 1925 visit and compromise -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaikom_Satyagraha
Left school after five years, joined family business at 12; married Nagammai at 19, she died 1933 -> https://ffrf.org/publications/day/periyar/

Self-Respect Movement 1925; Justice Party merged 1938; renamed Dravidar Kazhagam 1944, Periyar's term from 27 August 1944; Dravida Nadu demand; Maniammai leader 25 Dec 1973 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dravidar_Kazhagam

Self-respect marriages: no priests, holy fires or rituals subordinating the woman; legalised by Hindu Marriage (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act 1967 -> https://www.sabrangindia.in/article/self-respect-marriage-promise-equality-and-companionship

Title Periyar: women's conference, 13 November 1938, Chennai; resolution text -> https://thesouthfirst.com/tamilnadu/tamil-nadus-first-womens-conference-and-how-ev-ramasamy-naicker-became-thanthai-periyar/
Marriage 9 July 1949; Periyar 70, Maniammai 32; arrangement to secure property and trust -> https://feminisminindia.com/2021/01/06/periyar-maniammai-marriage/
28 June 1949 announcement; DMK founded 17 September 1949 -> https://www.thenewsminute.com/tamil-nadu/september-which-split-dravidians-periyar-weds-maniyammai-dmk-born-49850

Quotes 'He who created god is a fool, he who propagates god is a scoundrel, and he who worships god is a barbarian.', 'If there is no varnashrama dharma, there is no ground to talk about Hindu religion.', 'God and fate are the direct enemies of reason' (M. S. S. Pandian) -> https://scroll.in/article/871440/he-who-created-god-is-a-fool-periyar-believed-religion-and-rationality-are-complete-opposites

Madras High Court (Manikumar and Prasad JJ) dismissed PIL to remove inscriptions; found he declared from 1928 there is no God -> https://www.livelaw.in/amp/news-updates/right-to-disagree-with-existence-of-god-147845
Annihilation of Caste translated into Tamil with Periyar's help, published 1937 -> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annihilation_of_Caste
Met Ambedkar at his residence in Bombay, 6 January 1940 -> https://drambedkarbooks.com/2016/01/05/6th-january-1940-in-dalit-history-periyar-met-dr-ambedkar-at-mumbai
Never converted to Buddhism -> https://www.indianetzone.com/periyar_buddhism

1927 meeting with Gandhi; 'Gandhi Desh' after assassination; last speech Dec 1973 quote 'annihilation of God, annihilation of religion, annihilation of Gandhi, annihilation of Congress and annihilation of Brahmins' -> https://www.outlookindia.com/national/india-news-periyar-ev-ramasamy-the-man-who-opposed-mahatma-gandhis-idea-of-india-news-302169
1959 speech quote 'Brahminism came from Brahmins and hence it is the Brahmins who should be annihilated.' (P. A. Krishnan) -> https://pakrishnan.com/2018/02/19/test-1-2-3/

Supporter view: opposed brahminical authority, not individuals (Olivannan Gopalakrishnan, Inmathi, 18 Jan 2022) -> https://inmathi.com/2022/01/18/why-atheist-periyar-is-a-much-loved-icon-in-religious-tamil-nadu/38089/
Pillaiyar idol-breaking announced 27 May 1953 (Buddha Purnima), Bala Jeyaraman's biography via reader highlights -> https://www.goodreads.com/notes/26851211-periyar/21577671-aditya-bharadwaj?page=2

1971 Salem rally: competing versions; Periyar's audio account of slipper and Rama picture -> https://www.thenewsminute.com/amp/story/tamil-nadu/what-happened-periyars-salem-rally-1971-many-versions-116594
Seeman said Periyar 'insulted' Tamil (Dec 2024 event; Feb 2025 'will always oppose') -> https://www.thenewsminute.com/tamil-nadu/tn-will-always-oppose-periyar-and-his-ideology-says-seeman
